I graded 27 beauty SKUs and every single one was leaving somewhere between $2,400 and $45,000 on the table. The catch is the fix is different for every brand, so I stopped giving one-size advice and built a map instead.

It's two axes. Listing quality on one, catalog size on the other. Every brand lands in one of four boxes, and the box tells you the play, not the other way around.

High quality, low volume is the Catalog-Expansion Sprint, and Dove lives here. The listings are genuinely good, there just aren't enough of them, so you go wide and go fast.

High quality, high volume is Automation at Scale, where Maybelline sits, best in class at 84. When you're already good and already big, the only lever left is doing it faster than a human team ever could.

Low quality, high volume is Triage and Template, and that's Nivea's spot. Too many SKUs to hand-fix, so you build a template and stamp out the worst offenders first.

Low quality, low volume is White-Glove Uplift, which is Guerlain. Small catalog, weak listings, rebuild each one by hand.

The box that trips people up most is high/high, Maybelline's quadrant. Everyone assumes 'we're already good, we're basically done.' That's exactly the brand where automation prints the most, because good times big compounds. 

There is no one "best practice" for a catalog. Find your box first, then run the play.

The beauty brand leaving the most money on Amazon is the one you'd least expect. L'Oreal. $7.3M sitting on the table.

Not because they're bad at it. Because the biggest names have the most to lose, and right now almost none of them convert the demand they already have.

So we graded the real listings for the 10 biggest beauty brands, then ranked them by dollars left behind:

- L'Oreal: $7.3M
- Guerlain: $6.7M
- Lancome: $5.2M
- Estee Lauder: $4.4M
- all the way down to Pantene at $0.2M

Not one of the ten earned an A. The average listing is a 79. A B-.

57% of product searches begin on Amazon. The demand is already there. They are just losing it at the listing.

And here is the uncomfortable part of the ranking. The leak scales with size. The bigger and more "established online" the brand, the more it tends to leave behind, because one mediocre listing quietly caps a much larger catalog.

My pushback: stop scoring your Amazon presence by whether you show up. Score it by whether the listing wins.

Full ranking, every brand's score and the per-brand math in one report. Link in the comments.

Beauty is leaving $11.7B on the table online, and the brands supposedly winning the channel aren't actually good at it.

Across the 10 biggest beauty and personal-care companies, eCommerce is 25% of sales, but fair share, given where shoppers actually are, is 32% (FFA Consulting / Euromonitor). That 7-point gap is worth $11.7B in enterprise value today and $16.7B by 2030. 

Many will treat a number like that as a sales miss but it's a valuation miss and those are two very different conversations with your board.

So we pointed our grader at the top 10 beauty brands on Amazon to see who's converting the demand. Not one earned an A. The average listing came back at 79, which is a B-. 

Some of the brands with the most presence and the biggest budgets are turning in C+ homework...

The demand is sitting right there. 

My actual pushback: stop scoring your online business by revenue growth alone. Score it by whether your digital share matches where the category is headed, and whether the listings convert once people show up. 

We put the full leaderboard and the size-of-prize math into one report. Link in the comments.

What does OpenAI o1 mean for you as an AI builder or user?
 
1. First impressions
 
O1 or 'Strawberry' is incredibly powerful but not entirely new. It breaks down big tasks into smaller ones. For example, if you ask it to plan a trip to Mexico City, o1 will break that down into: pick a neighborhood, recommend hotels, and suggest restaurants. 
 
AI agent builders have been doing this for the past year. Pixii breaks down a request for an ad into design, artwork, writing, and more. MightyBot's UX was similar to o1: it explains the sub-tasks and tackles each one in order (e.g. find new sales leads from my emails and add them to Salesforce). We've also seen open source LLMs use this approach.
 
2. Why is o1 so powerful?
 
a. from 'Training' to 'Trying'
 
LLMs rely on massive 'pre-training'. This is akin to training a student for 12 years before letting them loose in the real world. OpenAI and others have already scraped the entire internet. Gains from pre-training are plateauing. 
 
o1 shifts the emphasis from training to "trying", where the agent learns by doing. For example, when planning a trip to Mexico City, the agent might try to find flights under $500 for this weekend. If it can't, it won’t stop—it’ll try different dates, check alternate airports, suggest adjusting the budget, or even explore buses. Every failed or successful attempt teaches it something new.
 
Tenacious models will try for longer and get more creative.
 
Currently the 'trying' phase lasts seconds. What if we let it try for months or years? What if we give it data and tools? That could lead to medical breakthroughs, trillion dollar businesses, and novel materials.
 
You might recognize this as optimization; the model searches for the best solution, learning from every move.
 
b. Force multiplier for your AI agent
 
AI agent builders previously had to create scaffolding for every step—choose neighborhood, pick hotel, and so on. Now, many of these smaller tasks can be handled with a single prompt to o1. 
 
Agent builders can focus their energy on the next level. Let O1 plan the trip. Your agent will book it across Expedia and Marriot, update your family's calendars, and email you with travel alerts and inspiration.
 
3. The new model reduces some problems and creates new ones
 
Problems reduced:
-rushing to an answer
-confusion
-hallucinations
 
Problems created:
-overthinking
-verbosity
 
4. "High-agency"
 
You want to hire high-agency people. The ones who 'figure it out'. They keep trying, get creative, and take work off your plate.
 
Same for AI agents.
